business_scope.primary_industry_name: Deep-Sea Tugboat Towage and Maritime Emergency Salvage Contracts

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Switzerland (Federal State; recommended cantonal seat: Zurich or Zug for the Aktiengesellschaft)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Germanic codified system based on Swiss Civil Code and Code of Obligations; public commercial law administered at federal and cantonal level)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (AMLA, SR 955.0, revised version in force from 1 Jan 2023); AMLA Ordinance (SR 955.01); Art. 305bis of the Swiss Criminal Code (SR 311.0); Art. 697j para 3 and Art. 928a of the Swiss Code of Obligations (SR 220, duty to maintain UBO register); Swiss Embargo Act (SR 946.231) and SECO sanctions regulations; Financial Market Infrastructure Act (SR 958.1) for FinSA/FinIA aspects

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized passport or identity document of ultimate beneficial owner (non-Swiss individual)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home country notary (e.g., Notary Public in the PRC or issuance authority) plus certified German/Italian/French translation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (China is a Hague Convention member since Nov 2023) or Consular Legalization for non-member states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation, Certificate of Good Standing / Excerpt from foreign commercial register of any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent foreign registry (e.g., Companies House UK, Hong Kong CR, or Singapore ACRA)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the corresponding competent authority (e.g., UK FCDO, HK HTU-STC)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Signed and notarized UBO declaration (Benefizialeigentümererklärung) per Art. 697j para 3 CO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Swiss notary or lawyer retaining power of attorney for incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the Federal Office of Justice (if the declaration is to be used abroad) or deposited with the cantonal commercial registry

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Audited or certified bank reference and funding confirmation for the minimum paid-up capital of CHF 100,000 (AG)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Swiss bank (SIX-transparent proof of capital) or licensed foreign correspondent bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille or bank attestation sent directly to the Swiss notary

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence (EDD) under AMLA includes screening of UBO, directors, and authorised signatories against UN consolidated sanctions lists, SECO Swiss sanctions list (including Russia- and OFAC-related designations applied through Swiss Embargo Act), EU consolidated list, OFAC SDN list, and international PEP databases (e.g., Dow Jones, World-Check). Given the Medium_Risk_Enhanced tier for maritime tug and salvage, additional adverse-media check and source-of-funds verification are required before signing the consent to incorporation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: ZEFIX – the Central Business Name Index (Zentraler Firmenindex) operated by the Swiss Federal Commercial Registry Office, accessible at zefix.ch; official filing through the cantonal Commercial Registry Office (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zürich or Zug)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A Swiss AG may register its name in German, French, Italian, or Romansh; legally binding records in ZEFIX must be in one official national language. Latin-script English names are admissible as supplementary text, but the legal-form suffix 'AG' or 'SA' must be in the registration language. No phonetic transliteration is required, but a transliteration into the official language must be added where the proposed name is in Chinese, Cyrillic, or other non-Latin script.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: 'Swiss', 'Schweizer', 'Eidgenossenschaft', 'Confédération' (requires Federal Council approval per Art. 51 HRegV)
'Trust', 'Trustee' (requires trust-license showing under the Federal Act on Trustees)
'Reederei', 'Marine', 'Salvage' (allowed only if the business license and actual activity substantiate deep-sea towage/salvage; otherwise deemed misleading)
Cantonal and communal coat-of-arms references (Art. 50 HRegV)
Abbreviations suggesting public-law status, or words implying state sponsorship without explicit consent
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The cantonal Commercial Registry Office must refuse a name that is misleading or creates confusion with existing entries (Art. 950 CO). Upon refusal, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal with the cantonal commercial register supervisory authority (Handelsregisteraufsichtsbehörde) within 30 days; the supervisory authority shall rule on the compliance of the name in accordance with Art. 960 CO. If the appeal fails, the applicant may appeal to the Federal Administrative Court (Bundesverwaltungsgericht). Only final and non-appealable registrations have binding effect.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible only on a limited basis: Swiss law (Art. 56 para 2 CO and Art. 15 HRegV) requires an actual executive administrative address in the canton of registration, where the entity genuinely keeps books and board decisions are effective. Pure letterbox / mail-forwarding arrangements without a verifiable physical presence are rejected by the registry's current practice (FOPO Circular). For an offshore towage holding company, renting a controlled serviced office with a Swiss resident director and local minutes-of-meeting will satisfy substance requirements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 15% baseline risk of an unannounced cantonal or federal UBO authenticity inspection in the first 36 months; increases to approximately 40% if the maritime towage licence and vessel registration trigger Swiss Flag State inspection under the Swiss Maritime Navigation Act, because domestic port state control may verify the AG's correspondence and management presence.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zürich or Cantonal Commercial Register of Zug
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registry tariff for AG incorporation (CHF 1,200–1,600)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce / Federal Commercial Registry Office

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market hourly rate benchmark for UBO screening and client onboarding (CHF 1,600–2,400)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Federal administrative fee and maritime license tariff for commercial vessels (approx. CHF 400)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Swiss tax registration, VAT (MWST) number and social security employer registration
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cantonal Tax Office and ESTV (Federal Tax Administration)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No statutory fee; external professional processing fee at market benchmark

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht, OR/SR 220), Articles 620-763 (Aktiengesellschaft); Commercial Registry Ordinance (HWO/SR 221.411) Arts. 52-65
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Swiss Commercial Registry (Handelsregisteramt) of the Canton of the Statutory Registered Office, supervised by the Federal Commercial Registry Office within the Swiss Federal Department of Justice and Police (FDJP)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Deed of Formation and Articles of Association (Statuten) with Director Acceptance Declarations
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum subscribed share capital is CHF 100,000 (OR Art. 621); at least 20% (CHF 20,000) must be fully paid in prior to registration and held in a blocked/escrow Swiss bank account evidenced by a banker's capital confirmation certificate (Kapitalbescheinigung)
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that this day of ____, the shareholders of the Company, acting as sole incorporators, adopt the Articles of Association of CH_AG (Swiss Code of Obligations Articles 620-650); RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office is irrevocably fixed in Switzerland at the address set forth in the Articles of Association; RESOLVED FURTHER, that the share capital of CHF 100,000, divided into 100 registered shares of CHF 1,000 each, is subscribed in full and paid in via blocked bank escrow; RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Name(s)] and [Name(s)] are elected as Directors with full powers of representation; RESOLVED FURTHER, that the officers of the Company are authorized to complete all commercial registry filings, bank formalities, and statutory publications.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarized Execution of Deed of Formation and Articles of Association with Name Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Notary Public competent for the registered office; name pre-check via Central Business Name Index (Zefix)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a pre-reservation search on zefix.ch. Draft the Deed of Formation and Articles of Association (Statuten) in accordance with OR Art. 626-638. Execute before a Swiss notary in the canton of the statutory registered office; the notary verifies the identity and legal capacity of every incorporator, the subscription of 100 registered shares of CHF 1,000 nominal each, and the compliance of the corporate purpose with ISIC 5222 deep-sea towage and maritime salvage contracts. The notary then issues the authentic instrument for filing.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney, if founders are represented
Valid passport or identity card of all shareholders and/or their legal representatives
Swiss or certified foreign address proof of each incorporator
Draft Articles of Association (Statuten)
Statement of corporate purpose consistent with deep-sea tugboat towage and maritime emergency salvage
Zefix name-reservation certificate or official name availability print-out
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses attestation or Zefix flags the corporate name as confusingly similar to an existing entity, adopt an alternative name from a pre-selected list and schedule a follow-up notarization within 3 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Share Capital Deposit with Swiss Bank and Blocked-Account Capital Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: FINMA-licensed Swiss Bank or other Swiss Licensed Financial Intermediary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked/escrow corporate account at a FINMA-licensed Swiss bank in the name of the company in formation. Transfer at least CHF 20,000 (20% of the CHF 100,000 subscribed capital; full payment recommended). The bank issues the formal capital confirmation certificate (Kapitalbescheinigung) verifying full payment and blocked status of funds for free disposal only after company registration; this certificate must accompany the commercial registry filing.
required_dossiers: Notarized deed of formation
Board/shareholder resolution approving full share subscription
Passport copies of all directors and ultimate beneficial owners
Capital deposit payment evidence (wire confirmation slip)
Swiss bank AML/KYC forms and source-of-funds declarations
Notarized Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests enhanced AML documentation, serve an additional source-of-funds affidavit supported by audited statements within 5 business days; absent bank clearance, engage an alternative FINMA-licensed bank with adjusted escrow terms or post a sworn capital funding declaration supported by independent audit confirmation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registry Filing, Legality Review and Registration Order
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized incorporation deed, Articles of Association, capital confirmation certificate, director acceptance declarations, specimen signature cards, and the U1 federal tax form through the cantonal commercial registry. The Registry performs a formal legality review under OR Art. 940. Upon clearance, the company receives its registration number (CHE-xxx.xxx.xxx) and the official commercial entity status becomes effective.
required_dossiers: Certified notarial deed of formation
Notarized Articles of Association (Statuten)
Bank capital confirmation certificate (Kapitalbescheinigung)
Written acceptances from all directors and authorized officers
Specimen signature cards of all signatories
Valid passport copies of all directors and shareholders
Commercial Registry statutory fee payment evidence (approx. CHF 800)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues an audit suspension or corrective notice (e.g. deficient articles, incomplete notarization, capital-evidence failure), submit a supplemental memorial and amended instrument within 10 days; where capital confirmation is challenged, request bank re-certification and serve the original mandate within the same period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal and Cantonal Tax, Social Security, VAT and Statistical Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA), Cantonal Tax Authority, SUVA, and State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply online for the company's UID enterprise number, VAT roll entry (mandatory when annual taxable turnover exceeds CHF 100,000), employer registration for OASI/DI/EO wage withholding, and compulsory accident insurance with SUVA. Register the enterprise in the federal business statistics and industry classification as ISIC 5222 / NAICS 488330 for deep-sea tugboat towage and salvage operations.
required_dossiers: Official Commercial Registry excerpt (Handelsregisterauszug)
Board resolution appointing tax, payroll and compliance officers
Directors' passport copies and Swiss residence permits or citizenship evidence
Statement of estimated turnover and ISIC 5222 corporate-purpose classification
Bank account details for VAT and social contribution debits
Completed UID and VAT application forms on the ESTV portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If ESTV or cantonal inquiry is extended, request an interim UID confirmation and re-submit the VAT application via the Federal Taxpayer Portal; payroll arrangements may operate conditionally with retroactive clearance and penalty exemption upon demonstrated good faith diligence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: SHAB Publication, Final Extract Issuance and Corporate Record Closure
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Official Gazette (Schweizerisches Handelsamtsblatt, SHAB) through the Federal Commercial Registry Publication Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The commercial registry automatically transmits the incorporation notice for SHAB publication. Verify the published particulars (company name, seat, share capital, directors and authorized signatories, corporate purpose). Retrieve the certified official extract (Handelsregisterauszug) from the Zefix portal, resolve any discrepancies, and archive certified copies for the maritime operating license, bank facilities, and contractual due diligence files.
required_dossiers: Commercial Registry registration number (CHE-xxx.xxx.xxx)
SHAB publication monitoring entry reference
No additional filing - registry-initiated publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the SHAB notice contains erroneous capital, seat, or representation particulars, apply for immediate rectification with the supporting authenticated registry excerpt pursuant to OR Art. 941; where third parties have relied on the erroneous publication, issue a corrective SHAB notice within 30 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Swiss Maritime Navigation Office of the Federal Office of Transport (Bundesamt für Verkehr, BAV), in coordination with the Basel-Rhine Maritime Port Authority and SECO Shipping Section
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Swiss Ship Operating License and Maritime Safety Certificate (Schifffahrtsgesetz SR 747.30; Schifffahrtsverordnung SR 747.301)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Swiss Federal Office for the Environment (BAFU/FOEN)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Conditional Registration - Category C (Operational Registration) for towage and salvage fleets without fixed shore installations; Full EIA required only if onshore support bases, dry-dock facilities, coastal infrastructure or fueling stations are constructed
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: MARPOL 73/78 Annexes I-VI compliance: no oil discharge permitted except via 15ppm oily water separator in international waters beyond 12 nautical miles; marine fuel sulphur content max 0.50% m/m (MARPOL Annex VI Reg. 14); NOx Tier II/III limits for marine diesel engines over 130 kW; bilge and wastewater discharges conform to Swiss Water Protection Act (GSchG) Art. 3 thresholds; ballast water treatment must meet IMO BWM D-2 biological standards

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification per cantonal civil defense fire-protection regulations; structural and load inspection of towing winches, towing hooks, and salvage cranes under BAV Marine Survey; workplace clearance and occupational medical fitness certificates issued by SUVA, with valid Swiss Occupational Safety Ordinance (SR 819.14) compliance and seafarer crew certificates of competence on board.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung – ESTV / Administration fédérale des contributions – AFC); official portal www.estv.admin.ch, with eVAT e-filing platform and e-services portal; UID registry administered by the Swiss Federal Statistical Office (BFS) at www.uid.admin.ch; customs export procedure administered by the Federal Office for Customs and Border Security (FOCBS/BAZG) through e-dec and the TARGO/Plate platform; cantonal tax administrations (Steuerämter) serve as collecting agents for cantonal and communal direct taxes under the federal harmonisation regime.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Swiss Aktiengesellschaft (AG): (1) incorporate in the commercial register (Handelsregister/Zefix) with minimum share capital of CHF 100,000 and a paid-up minimum of CHF 50,000; (2) obtain the statutory Swiss Business Identifier (UID – Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer) which is automatically issued by the Federal Statistical Office upon commercial register entry and is used as the cantonal corporate income tax number, federal tax number and VAT identification number (CHE-xxx.xxx.xxx); (3) for a foreign entity without a Swiss registered seat, obtain a UID by direct application through the ESTV eVAT registration portal or through the competent cantonal tax authority where the entity has a Swiss establishment; (4) register for VAT within 30 days of commencement of tax liability under Article 20 of the VAT Act, with mandatory appointment of a Swiss fiscal representative (Vertreter) for taxable persons not domiciled, resident or seated in Switzerland; the registration request is submitted electronically via eVAT and is effective from the date of registration; after approval the UID is activated for VAT purposes and the taxpayer is enrolled in the ESTV VAT register.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: the AG is a distinct legal taxpayer subject to Swiss corporate income tax at federal, cantonal and communal levels on its worldwide net profit and paid-in capital; profits attributable to foreign permanent establishments and foreign real estate are exempt under the territorial carve-out; the participation exemption and notional interest deduction only reduce the tax base; the AG is not a pass-through or transparent entity for Swiss tax purposes and cannot elect flow-through treatment; cross-border hybrid mismatch results are recharacterised under anti-hybrid rules introduced by the Federal Act on Tax Reform and AHV Financing (TRAF) effective 1 January 2020.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Switzerland does not operate a check-the-box election system. Available statutory elections applicable to an AG include: (a) VAT group taxation election under Article 13(2) VAT Act allowing legally, economically and organisationally integrated entities to form a single taxable person (Groupe TVA / Unternehmensgruppe); (b) election of the participation exemption at the cantonal level with requisite documentary evidence; (c) optional remuneration-neutral liquidation-style accounting for the corporate income tax; (d) the election for a foreign permanent establishment to be taxed in Switzerland on a treaty-exempt basis subject to the relevant double tax treaty; and (e) under hybrid mismatch rules no elective relief is available, the consequences being imposed by law (deduction denial or inclusion of income) without taxpayer election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Swiss Value Added Tax (Mehrwertsteuer / TVA / IVA) governed by the Federal Act of 12 June 2009 on Value Added Tax (VAT Act / LIVA) and the implementing VAT Ordinance (LIVE).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 annual taxable worldwide turnover for persons resident, domiciled or seated in Switzerland (Article 21(1) VAT Act); non-Swiss entities supplying taxable services in Switzerland are subject to mandatory registration without any turnover threshold pursuant to Article 21(3) VAT Act unless the Federal Tax Administration has granted an exemption under Article 21(5); voluntary registration is available under Article 21(4) where turnover is below the threshold; current federal rates applicable as of 1 January 2024 are 8.1% standard, 2.6% reduced, and 3.8% special accommodation rate; import VAT is collected by customs on importation into Swiss territory.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, API tax-stamping or digital seal system is operated by ESTV. Switzerland applies the QR-Bill (QR-Rechnung) payment standard for CHF-denominated invoices as of 1 January 2020, requiring a QR code and IBAN; the QR-Bill complements conventional e-invoicing formats (XML, ZUGFeRD/Swiss companion) and is accepted as evidence of remittance. With effect from 1 January 2026, Swiss Bundesrat ordinance requires domestic businesses to be able to receive B2B e-invoices in a structured electronic format, with SMEs required by 1 January 2027; exporters must retain electronic customs declarations via e-dec and may submit them via the digital TARGO/Plate platform; there is no requirement for customs declarations or invoices to pass fiscal clearance through ESTV before export.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating may be claimed for (i) export supplies of goods physically transported from Switzerland abroad under Article 52 VAT Act; (ii) transport and towage services supplied directly in connection with exported goods, including deep-sea towage and salvage services ancillary to such export, under Article 23(2)(4) VAT Act; and (iii) services performed or utilised outside Swiss territory, such as offshore towage and maritime salvage on the high seas, which are treated as outside the scope of Swiss VAT or zero-rated where the B2B place-of-supply rule locates the supply at the recipient's establishment abroad (Article 23(2)(6) VAT Act). To qualify, the invoice must be addressed to a foreign recipient, the service must be performed offshore or connected to goods leaving Switzerland, and the proceeds must be received from abroad; salvage or towage performed within Swiss territorial waters or for a Swiss-resident customer is taxable at 8.1%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (Ausfuhrzollanmeldung / déclaration d'exportation) lodged through e-dec and validated by FOCBS/BAZG with unique movement reference number (MRN) and export tariff line
Ocean bill of lading (Konnossement) or equivalent multimodal waybill / salvage service report evidencing cross-border carriage or offshore performance coordinates
Inward remittance certificate / SWIFT credit advice (Bankgutschrift) demonstrating receipt of foreign currency proceeds by the Swiss exporting entity from the foreign counterparty
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Federal Tax Administration audits verify export documents, bills of lading, customs declarations, and inward remittance evidence; records must be retained for 10 years. If the export zero-rating conditions are not substantiated or payment is not received within the 180-day period, ESTV retrospectively disallows the 0% rate and reassesses the supply at 8.1% VAT with default interest and late-payment interest. Standard assessment limitation is 5 years under Article 43 VAT Act, extended to 10 years in cases of deliberate evasion or tax fraud. Simple VAT violations carry fines up to CHF 25,000 under Article 182 VAT Act; aggravated VAT fraud under Article 183 VAT Act carries imprisonment up to 3 years and a fine up to CHF 30,000, with joint liability of the company and corporate officers. Fraudulent zero-rating claims also trigger anti-money-laundering reporting obligations and potential revocation of the Swiss fiscal representative mandate.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB / Schweizerische Nationalbank, Berne head office), acting with the Federal Department of Finance (FDF) and the State Secretariat for International Financial Matters (SIF); exchange-control and payment-policy supervision are exercised through the Foreign Exchange Ordinance (Devisenverordnung / Ordonnance sur les opérations de change, SR 941.131), while prudential and anti-money-laundering supervision of banks is exercised by FINMA (Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority) under the Banking Act of 8 November 1934 (BankG / SR 952.0) and the Anti-Money Laundering Act of 10 October 1997 (GwG / SR 955.0).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland maintains full and unrestricted convertibility of the Swiss franc on both current account and capital account under Article 1 of the Foreign Exchange Ordinance; no prior administrative authorization, central-bank approval, or exchange-control licence is required for cross-border payments, dividend distribution, capital repatriation, loan servicing, or settlement of maritime salvage and towage claims. The Swiss franc is freely floating and is not subject to any surrender or conversion quota. Practical frictions are limited to (i) the statutory 35% Swiss withholding tax on Swiss-source dividends, which can be reduced to a rate as low as 0% or partially refunded under an applicable double-taxation treaty where the beneficial owner qualifies, and (ii) the mandatory balance-of-payments statistical reporting obligation imposed on Swiss banks for individual cross-border transactions equal to or exceeding CHF 25 million per calendar month, which is a statistical disclosure duty rather than a restriction on convertibility. For a Swiss AG active in deep-sea towage and salvage, there is no exchange-control barrier to invoicing in CHF, EUR, or USD, nor to maintaining foreign-currency accounts at a FINMA-regulated bank.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. Switzerland imposes no statutory timeline for the repatriation of export earnings, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no obligation to bring foreign-currency export proceeds onshore. A Swiss Aktiengesellschaft (CH_AG) engaged in offshore towage and salvage may lawfully retain receivables denominated in CHF, EUR, or USD in domestic or foreign-currency accounts for an indefinite period. The only formalities are: (i) the company's annual financial statements must reflect the resulting currency exposure in accordance with Swiss GAAP FER; (ii) cross-border transactions at or above CHF 25 million in a calendar month must be reported by the instructing Swiss bank to the SNB in the balance-of-payments statistics; and (iii) proceeds received from salvage arbitration (e.g., Lloyd's Open Form awards) must be cleared through a Swiss-regulated payment channel to satisfy the enhanced due-diligence expectations of FINMA Circular 2016/07. There is no obligation to hedge, no conversion requirement at the time of receipt, and no penalty for holding export proceeds in a third currency.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: UBS Switzerland AG (Basel/Zurich, including the integrated former Credit Suisse franchise)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account for the statutory minimum share capital of CHF 100,000 (AG quota) plus a Multi-currency Operational Account (CHF/EUR/USD) with e-banking and corporate payment services; parallel access to a Master-Cash-Pooling arrangement for inbound salvage awards and outbound tug-boat disbursements.

Operational Account with domestic clearing (SIC) and foreign-currency sub-ledgers, Capital Pledged Account for registered share capital proof, and a treasury line for EUR/CHF and USD/CHF spot/forward execution; suitable for direct SEPA and Fedwire/CHIPS access.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque Cantonale Vaudoise (BCV, Lausanne, with maritime and trade-finance desk)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Trade Settlement and Escrow Account in CHF/EUR/USD supporting documentary letters of credit, Lloyd's Standard Form Wire settlement flows, and salvage-award collection under English law arbitration; marine-sector relationship banking team.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: BNP Paribas (Suisse) SA (Geneva, subsidiary of BNP Paribas Group)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account combined with a documentary credit facility (MT700 import/export letters of credit) and a foreign-exchange hedging facility for USD/EUR/CHF; particularly suited to Lloyd's Open Form (LOF) disbursements and P&I club settlements.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Domestic FINMA-licensed fintechs and neobanks, such as Yapeal, Swissquote, and neon, are rated Medium for treasury sub-functions (day-to-day liquidity, low-value SEPA payments, FX execution) and can be integrated as secondary accounts, but they do not provide documentary-credit capacity, escrow-settlement infrastructure, or Lloyd's salvage disbursement rails, and are therefore not viable as the primary banking relationship for a Medium-Risk-Enhanced ISIC 5222 entity. Foreign unauthorised e-money institutions and offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Wise, Revolut, Intergiro) are rated Low and are legally unattractive for a Swiss AG: FINMA treats unlicensed deposit-taking and payment intermediation as a regulatory offence, exposure to non-FINMA EMIs triggers enhanced due-diligence scrutiny under GwG Articles 3 and 8, and the absence of a Swiss settlement account (SIC membership or Swiss correspondent network) prevents compliant handling of LOF salvage awards and escrow disbursements. A hybrid stack is acceptable and common: Tier-1 Swiss bank for governance, escrow and clearing, plus one FINMA-licensed fintech for FX conversion and worker disbursements, provided the board's treasury policy explicitly limits both aggregate float and per-transaction limits.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Swiss law does not oblige every director of the CH_AG to appear physically before the bank; the mandatory requirement is the positive identification of the economic beneficial owner(s) and of each person holding signature authority, either by face-to-face meeting or by a FINMA-approved video-identification procedure in accordance with Article 9 of the AMLO-FINMA and FINMA Circular 2016/07. In practice, for a Medium-Risk-Enhanced maritime towage and salvage company, the onboarding bank will require at least one in-person interview in Switzerland (Zurich or Geneva) with the ultimate beneficial owner and at least one director with active signatory power, together with the notarised founding documentation; remote opening assisted by a Swiss-qualified lawyer or fiduciary is possible but the final risk decision will typically demand a physical meeting before account activation and before any inbound capital deposit is accepted. Post-opening treasury operations, wire releases, and FX orders may be handled fully through the bank's secure e-banking channel with dual authorisation, without further physical presence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and embargo screening failure: towage or salvage counterparties involving cargo owners, insurers, or P&I clubs registered in or trading with jurisdictions on the SECO (Swiss State Secretariat for Economic Affairs), OFAC, EU, or UN sanctions lists (e.g., Iran, Russia, North Korea, Syria, or occupied territories), which triggers an automatic mandate-refusal under GwG Article 9 and the Swiss Embargo Act.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Defensive documentation bundle: (i) a sanctions firewall matrix built from SECO, OFAC SDN, EU, and UN consolidated screening logs dated within 48 hours of the transaction; (ii) a full KYC and ultimate-beneficiary-owner declaration package for every vessel owner, cargo interest, and insurer involved in the specific towage or salvage contract; (iii) the executed salvage contract (LOF 2020 or BIMCO TOWCON form) naming the parties, the salvage vessel IMO number, and the geographical towage corridor; (iv) AIS track record and maritime casualty report for the distressed vessel; (v) written confirmation from the relevant P&I club that the casualty and award are covered; and (vi) the board resolution prohibiting any engagement with embargoed flags or sanctioned beneficial owners, submitted with a notarised signature specimen.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds opacity and third-party payment routing: salvage awards or towage hire received from a non-contractual third party, a shell intermediary in a low-tax jurisdiction, or through a chain of multiple correspondent banks, which the compliance officer flags as an unexplained third-party payment under GwG Articles 3 and 8 and FINMA Circular 2016/07 paragraph 25.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete source-of-funds audit trail: (i) original invoice and contract, including the Lloyds Standard Form of Salvage Agreement or BIMCO TOWCON, with the named remitter; (ii) the bank-secured MT103 remittance advice with the contractual reference and the exact purpose code; (iii) notarised declaration of origin of funds signed by the beneficial owner asserting the legal provenance of the capital, supported by the previous two years' audited financial statements of the CH_AG; (iv) charters, sub-contracts, and the salvage master's report evidencing the underlying service; and (v) written legal opinion from a Swiss or English maritime lawyer confirming the salvage award is an arm's-length commercial claim and not a conduit transaction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Corporate-veil and substance concerns: the entity is a newly formed Swiss AG with foreign shareholders and no physical office, employees, or operating assets in Switzerland, which triggers a 'round-tripping' or shell-company red flag and a demand for proof of economic substance under GwG Article 4 and FINMA Circular 2016/07 paragraph 44.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Substantive presence dossier: (i) certified extract from the Swiss Commercial Register (Handelsregister-Extract) showing the CH_AG's legal seat, purpose clause (offshore towage and salvage), and registered capital of CHF 100,000 fully paid in; (ii) lease agreement for a Swiss registered office and a client-side operational office; (iii) Swiss payroll records and social-insurance (AHV) confirmations for at least one resident director or local management; (iv) board minutes approving treasury policy, banking mandates, and the compliance manual; (v) a detailed business plan showing the towage vessel charter and salvage-operation pipeline; and (vi) audited (or review-opinion) annual financial statements demonstrating staff, premises, insurance premiums, and vessel-related expenditure traceable to Switzerland.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk geographic corridor concentration: towage operations touching conflict zones, piracy areas, or high-risk flags (e.g., Gulf of Guinea, Red Sea, Strait of Hormuz, or Marshall Islands/Cayman Islands shell registrations), which the Swiss bank's internal country-risk scoring treats as a Medium-Risk-Enhanced profile requiring heightened due diligence and possibly an escalation to the risk committee.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Geographic risk mitigation package: (i) a route-level risk matrix measuring UN, EU, and SECO embargo status, piracy insurance coverage, and flag-state attractiveness; (ii) certificates of sanctions screening for all vessels, owners, and charterers in the relevant corridor, freshly generated from a recognised screening database; (iii) the P&I club and hull-and-machinery insurance certificates, including war-risk and piracy endorsements; (iv) the specific towage contract appendices defining the transit corridor and the lawful cargo type; (v) if entering restricted waters, a written no-dealing representation from the charterer that neither the cargo nor the shipowner is connected to a sanctioned party, and (vi) a Swiss maritime counsel's legal opinion confirming that the salvage service does not constitute a re-export of strategic goods or a breach of Swiss embargo obligations.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound share-capital and shareholder-loan injections must be routed exclusively through a FINMA-regulated Swiss bank using SWIFT GPI (Global Payments Innovation) MT103 messages with explicit and non-manipulable purpose coding (e.g., 'CAPT - Equity Capital Contribution', 'Equity financing of salvage operations', or the ISO 20022 purpose 'MINI/CAPR') and full remitter identification including legal name, address, LEI, and tax identifier. The statutory capital of the CH_AG of at least CHF 100,000 (with minimum CHF 50,000 paid-in at incorporation) must be deposited into a dedicated capital-escrow account (Libor-/Einzahlungskonto) in the name of the company at the onboarding Tier-1 bank, evidenced for the commercial register by a bank confirmation (Bankbescheinigung) certifying that the funds are at the free disposal of the board. Shareholding documentation, a resolution of the extraordinary general meeting, the notarised subscription statement, source-of-funds declarations, and the UBO register extract must accompany the wire; in addition, the Swiss instructing bank will report the transaction to the SNB in the balance-of-payments statistics if the monthly cumulative cross-border flow equals or exceeds CHF 25 million. No exchange-control permission, SNB licence, or prior authorisation is required; the only admissible funding instruments are telegraphic transfer, SEPA credit transfer, Fedwire/CHIPS, and SWIFT MT103/202 cover, each with a matching purpose code and reconciled against the ledger as consolidated equity or subordinated shareholder loan.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for towage, salvage, wreck removal, fuel, port charges, and crew wages must be cleared through the following rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 single-customer transfers for operational payments and salvage-award disbursements to shipowners, insurers, and P&I clubs, with CHF clearing across SIX Interbank Clearing (SIC), EUR clearing via SEPA and T2 RTGS, and USD clearing via Fedwire or CHIPS through the Swiss bank's correspondent network; (ii) SWIFT MT700/MT710 documentary credits (commercial letters of credit) under UCP 600 for the reimbursement of tug-company hire and emergency-salvage commitments, issued or confirmed by the Tier-1 Swiss bank; (iii) the Lloyds Standard Form of Salvage Agreement (LOF) wire protocol, under which salvage awards agreed through the Lloyds Salvage Arbitration Branch or negotiated settlements are paid by escrow release instructions requiring dual board authorisation and a compliance attestation of the underlying award; and (iv) escrow disbursement instructions for multimillion-claim settlements, released only against a jointly signed SWIFT MT103 plus a written award notice and the bank's final sanctions screen. Aggregate outbound wires in a single currency equivalent to or above CHF 25 million per calendar month attract the same SNB statistical reporting duty, and every outbound USD wire must carry a correct SWIFT mandatory field 70 (remittance information) referencing the contract number and the salvage-master's report to prevent downgrade or interdict by a correspondent bank.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright OTC FX forwards in EUR/CHF and USD/CHF with a FINMA-regulated Swiss counterparty, executed under a validated ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with a Credit Support Annex and strictly within board-approved notional limits (no leverage above the underlying towage/salvage exposure).
FX swaps and roll-over swaps in USD/CHF, EUR/CHF, and EUR/USD used to fund daily operational liquidity mismatches without taking open speculative positions.
Cross-currency swaps (CCIRS) aligned with long-term ship-finance debt and charter-hire liabilities, converting USD or EUR debt service into CHF at fixed or floating rates.
Plain vanilla FX options (calls and puts) and zero-cost collars (risk reversals) covering salvage-award receipts and tug-charter disbursements for a horizon not exceeding 24 months.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on illiquid emerging-market currencies (e.g., NGN, BDT, IDR, EGP) that may arise from wreck-removal or port-state claims in developing jurisdictions, entered into with the Swiss bank's emerging-markets desk and subject to SECO/OFAC/EU sanctions screening of both the counterparty and the reference currency.

Interest rate swaps (IRS) associated with the underlying vessel-financing facility, considered permissible treasury tools when used strictly for liability management of the CH_AG's maritime loan book, and excluded from propriety trading by a written treasury policy approved by the board.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting (AGM) protocol and resolutions for adoption of annual financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders; not filed with Commercial Register unless resolutions amend articles or change board members
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AGM must convene within 6 months after the fiscal year-end; calendar year companies must hold by June 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct government filing; failure to approve accounts can trigger civil liability and tax office inquiries; persistent non-compliance may lead to court-ordered dissolution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory financial statements including balance sheet, income statement, and notes (Anhang)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/SIF) and Cantonal Tax Authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual corporate tax return and financial schedules due within 6 months of fiscal year-end or by March 31 for calendar-year companies; extensions up to 3 months in certain cantons
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties (Verspätungszuschlag) up to CHF 10,000; default tax assessment based on estimated income; interest at 4% per annum; repeated default may trigger administrative enforcement

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT return (if taxable turnover exceeds CHF 100,000)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Federal Tax Administration ESTV - Switzerland VAT
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Quarterly or semi-annual deadlines depending on turnover; for annual filers, return and payment due 60 days after fiscal year-end (or per ESTV schedule)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty up to 3% of unpaid VAT with no reduction on late remittance; default interest at 4%–5%; possible criminal penalties for deliberate evasion

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Social security wage and insurance declarations (AHV/AVS, SUVA, BVG)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Social Insurance Office (BSV) / Compensation Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Deathline monthly, quarterly, or annual, by the 10th of the month following the settlement period; annual wage summary by January 31 following the reporting year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest at 5% per annum; late payment surcharge of 5% of unpaid contribution; repeated default triggers administrative fines and employer liability

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary audit (Ordentliche Revision) required if for two consecutive fiscal years any two thresholds are exceeded: balance sheet total CHF 20 million, annual turnover CHF 40 million, 250 full-time equivalent employees. Otherwise, the AG may opt for an 'opting-out' audit (Small AG) or an 'opting-up' restricted audit (Eingeschränkte Revision) if shareholders unanimously agree and the company has fewer than 10 full-time employees.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations (OR) financial reporting requirements; IFRS or Swiss GAAP FER may be adopted for statutory or consolidation purposes; listed companies must apply IFRS or Swiss GAAP FER (as permitted).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Switzerland maintains no public annual UBO filing for ordinary AGs. However, the company must maintain an internal register of the ultimate beneficial owners of shares exceeding 25%, as well as a share register (Aktienbuch) recording owners of registered shares. Under the revised Anti-Money Laundering Act, legal entities must disclose UBO information to financial intermediaries upon request. Any transfer of shares involving registered shares is recorded in the share register; no annual confirmation to a central registry is required.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Aktienbuch / Register of Shareholders)
Register of Directors (Board minutes and director appointments)
Minute Book (Minutes of Annual General Meeting and Board Meetings)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,500 - USD 4,000 per annum for a professional registered office or corporate agent in Switzerland
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000 - USD 25,000 per annum for a statutory audit of an AG depending on size; USD 2,500 - USD 5,000 for small companies qualifying for opting-out or restricted audit

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 8.5% federal corporate income tax (imposed on profit after tax; combined Zug cantonal/municipal effective rate approx. 11.5%–12.0% on pre-tax profit)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Swiss-flag deep-sea towing and salvage income is exempt from federal, cantonal, and communal tax under the Federal Act on Maritime Navigation and Art. 71 DBG; participation exemption for qualifying dividend and capital-gain income (≥10% participation or ≥CHF 1 million market value); Zug patent box and notional interest deduction may further reduce the effective rate; cantonal holding privilege available for qualifying holding AGs.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Combined federal and cantonal corporate income tax return — 'Steuererklärung für juristische Personen' (Form 2010/2), filed electronically via the eTax Zug portal (www.zg.ch/steuern) or the unified Swiss tax administration portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within six months after the financial year-end; for a 31 December year-end the filing deadline in Canton Zug is 30 June of the following year; written extension requests may be granted only prior to the deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box A – Angaben zur juristischen Person
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered legal name, Swiss UID number, registered office, legal form 'Aktiengesellschaft', commercial register file number, date of incorporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The AG files as the Swiss-resident taxpayer; foreign shareholders are not entry filers unless they are managing officers requiring the controlling-shareholder annex (Form B).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal-year opening and closing dates, gross turnover, total income, and profit or loss before tax as derived from the statutory financial statements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Worldwide income of the Swiss-resident AG is prima facie taxable; no group or consolidated taxation is available to a foreign corporate parent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Depreciation of tugboats, salvage cranes, and auxiliary vessels; provisions for wreck-removal guarantees and contingent salvage claims; entries must comply with commercial and tax accounting rules (Art. 62–64 DBG).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Vessels under foreign flag or bareboat-chartered back to the parent are scrutinised; charter-party and vessel registration certificates must be attached.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Dividends and capital gains from qualifying participations (≥10% of share capital or ≥CHF 1 million market value) for which the participation relief is claimed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the exempted income derives from a low-tax affiliate lacking substance, reclassification as a hidden profit distribution will be asserted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-backs for non-arm's-length related-party invoicing, excessive management fees, interest on shareholder debt economically treated as equity, and unreported constructive dividends.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Constructive distributions to non-resident shareholders are subject to the 35% Swiss withholding tax on the grossed-up amount.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box F – Steuerbarer Gewinn und Steuerbares Eigenkapital
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final taxable profit after deduction of loss carryforwards (maximum 7 years), and taxable equity used to compute the cantonal/municipal capital tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The taxable-equity figure must reconcile with the statutory balance sheet; thin-capitalisation reclassification of excessive related-party debt is a standard audit adjustment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing after a formal reminder triggers a procedural fine (Ordnungsbusse) of up to CHF 10,000 under Art. 174 DBG, default interest of approximately 4.5% per annum on the unpaid liability, and, in the case of wilful non-filing, criminal prosecution with a fine of up to one-third (or two-thirds in aggravated cases) of the evaded tax; cantonal collection costs are added.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Swiss withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) quarterly return — Form 102 'Verrechnungssteuer-Abrechnung' filed electronically with the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) via the SURE-VST e-portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 30 days after the end of the calendar quarter in which a taxable distribution (including hidden distributions) was made (Art. 11 VStG).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All dividends, constructive dividends, bonus shares, and deemed distributions paid on the share capital, with recipient name, residence, and shareholding percentage.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For foreign recipients, the applicable DTA rate must be verified; the AG must hold the recipient's Form 82 before applying any treaty-reduced refund procedure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest on Swiss-resident bond issues, money-market instruments, and hybrid debt instruments classified as taxable note interest.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ordinary intercompany loans and bank credit are outside the WHT net; only bond and money-market interest is taxed at 35%, subject to DTA refund.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation and remittance of the 35% tax to the ESTV; if the shareholder contractually receives a net amount, the AG must gross up and cannot deduct the WHT notionally.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Failure to gross up and remit exposes the AG to a deficiency assessment on the full gross amount plus penalty interest.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Non-remittance or late remittance triggers default interest (currently 4.5% per annum) and criminal sanctions under Art. 69–70 VStG, including a fine of up to one-third of the tax due for intentional evasion; vessels and escrow accounts may be seized to secure the claim.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Swiss VAT return — 'Mehrwertsteuer-Abrechnung' (Form 603/605) filed through the ESTV e-portal 'eMWST'.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: By the 60th day after the end of the calendar quarter; annual filing option for entities with an input-tax surplus and turnover below CHF 5 million (subject to prior approval).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross consideration for towage, salvage, wreck-removal, and emergency assistance; international high-seas and vessel-connected services are zero-rated.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the AG imports towage-management services from the foreign parent, the reverse-charge mechanism applies; VAT refunds are not claimable by a non-resident service provider absent Swiss residency.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Input VAT on bunkering, hull repair, port-state charges, and third-party management services, deductible only where the invoice is issued to the Swiss AG and the service is actually rendered.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Invoices issued by related foreign parties are disallowed if they lack economic substance or fail the arm's-length requirements.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late payment draws interest at 4.5% per annum; intentional VAT evasion is punished with a fine of up to one-third of the evaded tax in addition to reassessment; the VAT claim is a privileged claim ranking over unsecured creditors.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% gross withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) on distributions from a Swiss AG; Swiss-resident shareholders receive a full credit or refund; foreign beneficial owners may claim a refund down to the applicable DTA rate, generally 0%–15%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The foreign recipient files Form 82 'Antrag um Rückerstattung der Verrechnungssteuer' with the ESTV within three years after the end of the calendar year of payment (Art. 32 VStG). The form must be countersigned by the foreign tax authority as a Tax Residency Certificate (Ansässigkeitsbescheinigung), accompanied by the dividend voucher and, for tiered structures, the full intermediary certification. New-generation DTAs with principal-purpose-test clauses require a beneficial-ownership and substance declaration; refunds are paid in Swiss francs without interest and may be withheld where the recipient lacks economic substance.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: domestic withholding tax is 0% on licence fees paid to non-residents; treaty rates are typically 0%–5%. Interest: ordinary intercompany loan and bank credit interest is outside the Swiss WHT net (0% statutory), while interest on Swiss-resident bond and money-market instruments is subject to 35% WHT, reduced by DTA to 0%–10%; thin-capitalisation reclassification of excess related-party debt converts the disallowed excess into a deemed dividend chargeable at 35% WHT.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory country-by-country reporting for Swiss-parented MNE groups or constituent entities of a foreign group with consolidated group revenue of at least CHF 900 million; Switzerland imposes no fixed statutory Local File/Master File monetary threshold at the taxpayer level, but the tax administration may order documentation on a risk basis; for maritime towage and salvage entities a contemporaneous OECD-compliant transfer-pricing study is strongly advised where intercompany turnover exceeds CHF 1 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland applies an economic-substance doctrine through the Federal Act on Maritime Navigation — Swiss flag registration, statutory seat, and effective general management in Switzerland are preconditions for the direct-tax shipping exemption; under the OECD Inclusive Framework and modern LOB/PPT clauses in Swiss DTAs, a shell AG holding passive towage contracts for a foreign parent is denied treaty relief, the 35% WHT is reimposed, and the maritime tax privilege is retroactively revoked.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate under-declaration of towage and salvage revenue, overstatement of bunkering or crew costs, forged voyage logbooks and invoices, or repeated failure to file after a formal reminder.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment through the extended limitation period (10 years for wilful concealment); penalty of one-third of the evaded federal and cantonal tax, increased to two-thirds for forged documents (Art. 175 DBG); tax fraud (Art. 186 DBG) carries imprisonment up to 2 years or a fine up to CHF 10,000; the vessel may be subject to maritime arrest to secure the tax claim.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed or tolerated the false declaration are criminally liable as organs (Art. 12 DBG), expose themselves to personal imprisonment and fines, and are jointly and severally liable for civil restitution of the evaded tax under Art. 754 OR; Swiss tax-criminal procedure permits exit bans for defendants domiciled abroad and seizure of private bank accounts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Treaty-Shopping / Lack of Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: An AG registered in Zug but wholly managed and economically controlled from a foreign towage group; no local board meetings, no Swiss employees, no operational marine office; routing of transparently foreign salvage contracts through the Swiss entity solely to obtain the 0% DTA dividend rate or the shipping tax exemption.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of Swiss tax residency and treaty benefits; reassessment of revenue in the hands of the foreign principal; retroactive application of the 35% WHT on all distributions; exchange of information under the Swiss Mutual Assistance Act; deregistration of the Swiss-flag vessel and revocation of the navigation licence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The board may be sued for the unpaid WHT and taxes for breach of corporate purpose (Art. 717 OR); directors who knowingly enabled the artificial structure face criminal sanctions for false attestations, can be struck from the commercial register with a prohibition on future mandates, and may be subjected to exit restrictions and extradition risks under the Swiss Criminal Procedure Code.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Billing the foreign parent below market for emergency salvage and towing capacity; paying excessive management, safety, or IT fees to a zero-tax related entity; absence of written intercompany service agreements; circular Escrow payment flows.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Arm's-length adjustment with reclassification of the shortfall as a hidden dividend subject to 35% WHT plus default interest; an intentional mispricing penalty of up to one-third of the evaded tax (Art. 175 DBG); the cantonal tax authority may issue a documentation order with daily fines for late delivery.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approved non-arm's-length contracts are personally liable for the resulting tax shortfall and WHT under Art. 754 OR; in cases of falsified invoices, directors face tax-fraud imprisonment and a personal fine; the foreign parent is indirectly exposed through Swiss enforcement proceedings.
